title: The action-groupoid presentation of a quotient morphism after object base change
statement:
Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A groupoid in algebraic spaces has the operations and test-point laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], with algebraic spaces in place of schemes. For any such groupoid $(U,R)$ write $[U/R]$ for the stackification of its test-point groupoid on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Let $(f_0,f_1):(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)\to(U',R',s',t',e',i',c')$ be a morphism of groupoids over $S$, meaning maps on objects and arrows commuting with all operations. It induces a morphism $[f]:[U/R]\to[U'/R']$. Put $A=U\times_{f_0,U',t'}R'$ and $B=R\times_{f_0s,U',t'}R'$. Give $A$ its map to $U'$ by $(u,r')\mapsto s'(r')$. On $B$ define source $(r,r')\mapsto(s(r),r')$, target $(r,r')\mapsto(t(r),c'(f_1(r),r'))$, unit $(u,r')\mapsto(e(u),r')$, inverse $(r,r')\mapsto(i(r),c'(f_1(r),r'))$, and composition $((r_1,r'_1),(r_2,r'_2))\mapsto(c(r_1,r_2),r'_2)$ for composable arrows. These operations make $(A,B)$ a groupoid over $U'$, and its quotient has a canonical equivalence
$$[A/B]\simeq U'\times_{[U'/R']}[U/R]$$
commuting with the maps to $U'$ and $[U/R]$. The comparison sends $(u,r')$ to $(s'(r'),u,r':s'(r')\to f_0(u))$. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the sheaf fibre products $A$ and $B$ are algebraic spaces. Write $P=[U/_{p}R]$ and $P'=[U'/_{p}R']$ for the fibred groupoids of test points before stackification. The maps $f_0,f_1$ define a functor $P\to P'$, since they commute with all operations. Let $D$ be the discrete fibred groupoid of the sheaf $U'$, with the functor $D\to P'$ sending $u'$ to the corresponding object. Form the fibrewise $2$-product $K=D\times_{P'}P$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 04Y4 (lemma-cartesian-square-of-morphism), construction preceding the lemma and its proof.

proof.text: An object of $K(T)$ is $(u',u,r')$ with $s'(r')=u'$ and $t'(r')=f_0(u)$. Forgetting $u'$ gives a bijection with $A(T)$, with inverse $(u,r')\mapsto(s'(r'),u,r')$. An arrow from $(u'_2,u_2,r'_2)$ to $(u'_1,u_1,r'_1)$ has first component the identity (thus $u'_2=u'_1$) and second component $r:u_2\to u_1$, satisfying $c'(f_1(r),r'_2)=r'_1$. It is therefore uniquely the pair $(r,r'_2)\in B(T)$ with the source and target in the statement. Conversely any such pair supplies this arrow, since $s'(c'(f_1(r),r'_2))=s'(r'_2)$. This is exactly the arrow compatibility equation of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 04Y4 (lemma-cartesian-square-of-morphism), construction preceding the lemma and its proof.

proof.text: Under these bijections the identity is $(e(u),r')$. Inversion is $(i(r),c'(f_1(r),r'))$, because $c'(f_1(i(r)),c'(f_1(r),r'))=r'$. For composable pairs one has $s(r_1)=t(r_2)$ and $r'_1=c'(f_1(r_2),r'_2)$; their composite is $(c(r_1,r_2),r'_2)$, since $c'(f_1(r_1),r'_1)=c'(f_1(c(r_1,r_2)),r'_2)$. These are the unit, inverse and composition laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. The operations are natural in $T$ and hence are maps of the algebraic-space sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Their laws hold because these formulas identify them with the groupoid operations in $K(T)$. Both ends have the same $s'(r')$, so the groupoid is over $U'$. The bijections and their inverses commute with restrictions; thus the raw test-point groupoid of $(A,B)$ is isomorphic to $K$, preserving both projections and the comparison arrow $r'$.

source.place: Tag 04Y4 (lemma-cartesian-square-of-morphism), construction preceding the lemma and its proof.

proof.text:
The discrete fibred groupoid $D$ is an fppf stack: the sheaf condition for $U'$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] glues its objects, and its only arrows are identities, so descent cocycles are precisely equality on overlaps. Apply [lem-sfb-stackification-two-fibre-products] on the big fppf site, retaining $D$ as its own stackification. The raw identification above gives
$$[A/B]\simeq a(K)\simeq D\times_{a(P')}a(P)=U'\times_{[U'/R']}[U/R].$$
Here the quotients are exactly the stackifications of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. The comparison in the cited theorem extends the raw triple functor, so on $(u,r')$ it is $(s'(r'),u,r')$; its projections are the map to $U'$ and the quotient morphism induced by $(A,B)\to(U,R)$. The same compatibility identifies the right-hand map with $[f]$. This proves the stated $2$-commutativity and equivalence without assumptions on the source or target maps beyond the groupoid laws.
